security_audit.summary: AI review confirmed critical supply-chain risk from curl-to-shell installer instructions and shell-derived binary downloads. Many Markdown backtick and documentation URL matches are false positives, but the skill also documents cloud uploads of local files and social media actions. No prompt injection attempt was found.

remediation.suggestion: Remove curl-to-shell instructions. Use signed package manager installs or checksum-verified downloads that require explicit user approval before execution.
Replace command substitution that parses a remote manifest with fixed release assets, signed metadata, or an official installer with clear verification steps.
Require explicit user consent before uploading local paths. Reject parent-directory, home-directory, and broad absolute paths unless the user approves them.
Require confirmation before commands that post, message, follow, like, or retweet. Show the account, action, content, and target first.

semantic_findings.title: Automatic Local File Uploads to Cloud Apps
semantic_findings.description: The instructions state that URL fields also accept local paths and that the CLI automatically uploads those files. This can expose sensitive local files to inference.sh if an agent selects paths without explicit user consent.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The files explicitly describe automatic upload of local paths, including absolute, parent-directory, and home-directory examples. The behavior is central to the documented workflow.

semantic_findings.title: Automated Social Media Account Actions
semantic_findings.description: The skill advertises Twitter/X automation and examples for posting media. Commands can post, send messages, follow, like, or retweet through external apps without a built-in confirmation step.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The capability is directly listed in the skill examples and available categories. Legitimate use is possible, but unintended account actions are a clear business-logic risk.

content.user_title: Run AI Apps with inference.sh CLI
content.value_statement: AI workflows often require separate APIs for images, video, search, and language models. This skill helps Claude, Codex, and Claude Code discover and run inference.sh apps through the belt CLI.
actual_capabilities: List and search inference.sh apps by category, name, featured status, or release order.
Inspect app details, including input and output schema information.
Generate sample input files for selected apps before execution.
Run image, video, language, search, audio, 3D, and utility apps through belt.
Track long-running tasks and retrieve saved results by task ID.
Use local file paths as app inputs when the CLI supports upload.
limitations: The belt CLI must be installed and authenticated before most workflows work.
App availability, pricing, quotas, and output quality are controlled by inference.sh.
Local file paths may upload files to cloud services, so users must approve each path.
The skill does not run AI models offline or provide local GPU execution.

use_cases.title: Create Media Assets
use_cases.description: Generate images, videos, audio, or avatars from a consistent CLI workflow.

use_cases.title: Prototype AI Workflows
use_cases.description: Compare app schemas, generate sample inputs, and test cloud AI tasks quickly.

use_cases.title: Search and Analyze Information
use_cases.description: Run hosted search and language apps for research, summaries, and structured answers.

prompt_templates.title: Find Useful Apps
prompt_templates.prompt: Use infsh-cli to find image generation apps for product mockups. Show useful options and explain when to choose each one.

prompt_templates.title: Prepare Sample Input
prompt_templates.prompt: Use infsh-cli to inspect google/veo-3-1-fast and create a sample input plan for a short product video. Ask before running it.

prompt_templates.title: Run and Track a Task
prompt_templates.prompt: Use infsh-cli to run falai/flux-dev-lora for this image idea: [describe image]. Track the task and summarize the result location.

prompt_templates.title: Compare a Full Workflow
prompt_templates.prompt: Use infsh-cli to compare two image apps and two video apps for a launch campaign. Include inputs, workflow steps, and safety checks.

output_examples.input: Find image generation options for a fast concept art workflow.
output: A short list of matching image apps by speed and quality.
A recommendation for the first model to test.
Notes about required prompt fields and expected media output.

output_examples.input: Run a long video generation task and check it later.
output_examples.output: The assistant submits the task, records the task ID, checks status later, and summarizes the final video result location.

output_examples.input: Prepare a safe local media upload.
output: A request for approval before any local file is uploaded.
A clear list of selected file paths.
A warning when a path points outside the working directory.

best_practices: Inspect app details and sample inputs before running a new app.
Ask for user approval before uploads, social actions, or long-running paid tasks.
Store API keys securely and avoid placing secrets in prompts or saved input files.
anti_patterns: Do not run installer commands from remote scripts without verification.
Do not upload broad local paths, parent directories, or private files without consent.
Do not post, message, follow, like, or retweet without a final user confirmation.

faq.question: What CLI does this skill use?
faq.answer: It uses the inference.sh belt CLI to discover apps, run tasks, and retrieve task results.

faq.question: Do I need an inference.sh account?
faq.answer: Yes. Most commands require the CLI to be installed and authenticated with an account or API key.

faq.question: Can it generate images and videos?
faq.answer: Yes. The references list image, video, audio, language, search, 3D, and utility app categories.

faq.question: Can it use local files?
faq.answer: Yes. Some apps accept local paths, and the CLI uploads those files to cloud services.

faq.question: Does it run models locally?
faq.answer: No. It submits jobs to inference.sh cloud apps and returns task outputs or hosted file links.

faq.question: What should I confirm before running commands?
faq.answer: Confirm uploads, paid or long-running tasks, social media actions, and any installation or update command.
